solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spicy chop cooked with a pinch of tarragon in mixed stew?

indicators.note: cooking works ingredients over, so the word before it is rearranged
a pinch is only a tiny amount, so just the opening letter of the herb is used

blocks.note: spicy food is hot
the word chop rearranged
first letter of tarragon

explanation.surface: A recipe: a peppery chopped stew finished with a little tarragon.
explanation.walkthrough: HOTCHPOT is the older form of hotchpotch; the question mark admits the definition is a figurative 'mixed stew'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotchpot is a jumble or mixture of things, originally a pot of mixed meats and vegetables.

clue.text: Small window that is round (seen from below), befouled badly

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the bottom up runs the letters backwards
something done badly is botched and disordered, so the letters of the preceding word are jumbled

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
O is round in shape
the letters of befouled rearranged

explanation.surface: A little round window has been badly fouled, by birds perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The French name means 'bull's eye'; IE and O are read upwards before the jumbled befouled follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An oeil-de-boeuf is a small round or oval window, typically set high in a wall or roof.

clue.text: Pedigree chestnut, say

blocks.note: first meaning: a family ..., a line of ancestry
second meaning: a chestnut is one example of this kind of plant

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pedigree chestnut horse; 'say' marks chestnut as just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A family tree charts a pedigree, and the chestnut is a type of large woody plant with a trunk.

clue.text: Ornamental pendant with doubled opener requiring customs certificate

indicators.note: the first letter is swapped so that it repeats a letter found later in the word

blocks.note: a locket is a pendant worn on a chain

explanation.surface: A jeweller's pendant with a two-part catch needs paperwork at customs.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the L of LOCKET to C, so that the opener matches the C in the middle and C appears twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocket was the seal of the King's custom-house, and so a document certifying that duty had been paid.

clue.text: Husband roared wildly for e.g. caviar (7, two words)

indicators.note: acting wildly is acting without order, so the letters of the verb before it are scrambled

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
roared rearranged

explanation.surface: A husband bellowed furiously when served caviar.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard roe is the mass of eggs of a female fish, and caviar is sturgeon's eggs, so it is one instance.

clue.text: Silly old character, soft on top

definitions.note: used as a noun: a silly person

indicators.note: in a down entry, being on top means coming first in the word

blocks.note: p (piano) means soft in music
a rune is a letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone describes a foolish old eccentric who has gone soft in the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun here, as in 'you silly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prune is slang for a dull or foolish person, much the same as calling someone a silly.

clue.text: Producing hormones secreting what's central to good blending

indicators.note: the centre of the next word is taken, its two middle letters
blending mixes things together, so the gathered letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the middle pair of good

explanation.surface: A gland description: it produces hormones by secreting a good blend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secreting' looks like a biological verb in the surface but is simply anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Oestrogenic means generating oestrogen, the female sex hormone, so it describes producing hormones.

clue.text: Prohibition? It's essential to deprive topers

indicators.note: the essence or core of the following words holds the letters we want

blocks.note: found running across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A temperance argument: banning drink is vital to stop drunkards.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at Prohibition, the US alcohol ban; the question mark warns it means any ban.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is a formal prohibition, the power or act of forbidding something.

clue.text: Computer girl' put on exercises to get fit?

indicators.note: in a down entry, one part put on another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: Ada is a girl's name and a computer programming language
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: A girl at a computer is told to do some exercises to get in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get fit' suggests exercise, but 'fit' is the verb meaning to make suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt something is to make it suitable for a new purpose, to fit or adjust it.

clue.text: Period instruments decorative band holds slantwise mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word before it is dropped
one thing holding another wraps around it

blocks.note: a tie is a decorative band worn round the neck
on the bias means slantwise, diagonally

explanation.surface: Early-music players in a band wear decorative ribbons hung at a slant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period instruments' suggests early music and is right in a literal way: the tibia was an ancient Roman flute, also the name of the shin bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibiae is the plural of tibia, a pipe or flute of ancient Greece and Rome, so instruments of a past period.

clue.text: Self-denial time in shoddy acts rejected — it's star quality I'm after (11, two words)

indicators.note: shoddy work is badly put together, so the next word's letters come out disordered
one part placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: acts rearranged
Lent is the season of fasting before Easter
something rejected is thrown out

explanation.surface: Someone sitting through weak acts at an audition is hunting for real stars.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in the first person: the speaker is the one looking for star quality, so the answer is who is talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent scout seeks promising performers, so star quality is what such a person is looking for.

clue.text: We're promised Jock's alleged tantrums

blocks.note: pled is the Scots past tense of plead, to allege; Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman
gee is Scots for a fit of temper, the Scots marker carrying over

explanation.surface: Someone claims a Scotsman's tantrums were promised to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jock's' governs both words that follow: each is a Scots usage, so the solver must think in dialect for both.
explanation.definitionFit: Pledgees are people to whom a pledge is given, so they can say that something was promised to them.

clue.text: Temple-shaped monuments, old, protected by Greek goddess

indicators.note: something protected is shielded on both sides by its guardian, so it goes inside

blocks.note: Hera was queen of the Greek gods
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Old temple-like memorials stand under the protection of a Greek goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroa is the plural of heroon, a shrine or monument shaped like a temple and raised to a hero.

clue.text: Regiment given mug, therapeutic

blocks.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps
mug and dial are both slang for the face

explanation.surface: A regiment is presented with a mug, which apparently works as a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a cup but means the face, as does dial.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedial means intended to cure or put right, which is exactly what a therapeutic treatment does.

clue.text: Chippendale item, item that's bust at left and right, cracked inside (13, two words)

indicators.note: a cracked thing is broken apart, so the gathered letters before it are rearranged
the shuffled group goes inside the first word

blocks.note: a piece is an item; this is the second of the two items in the clue
taken as written
taken as written
L is short for left
R is short for right

explanation.surface: A Chippendale antique is described as broken at both ends and cracked in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'cracked' does that job. Chippendale was an 18th-century English furniture maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A piecrust table is a small round tripod table with a raised carved rim, a classic Chippendale design.

clue.text: Convalescence is lost after constant card sets

indicators.note: what is lost is no longer there, so those letters are removed from the longer word
coming after places the shortened word behind the single letter

blocks.note: c is the symbol for a constant such as the speed of light
anastasis is a rare word for convalescence
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recovering patient loses at cards after constantly playing them.
explanation.walkthrough: Anastasis is a rare Chambers word, from the Greek for rising up, which is why the convalescence block is hard to find.
explanation.definitionFit: In the game canasta, a canasta is a meld of seven or more cards of the same rank, so it is a set of cards.

clue.text: One entering dressed in vestment that's taken off

indicators.note: something entering goes inside what follows

blocks.note: a cope is a long cloak worn by clergy, so coped means wearing one
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A priest dons a vestment and later removes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken off' suggests undressing, which suits the vestment, but it means mimicked.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off someone is to imitate or mimic them, and copied means imitated.

clue.text: Sticker at 18 Across? Right!

blocks.note: ad is Latin for at or to
this entry is the very place in question, so here
R is short for right

explanation.surface: A note asks whether a label belongs at this spot, and confirms it does.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue points to its own number: 18 Across is this light, so it means here.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherer is someone or something that sticks, whether to a surface or to a cause.

clue.text: Apollyon, gee calling for a flutter in Bangkok?

definitions.note: the definition describes a coin by its use, a small stake for a bet in Thailand

blocks.note: Apollyon is a name for the Devil in Revelation and Pilgrim's Progress
gee is how the letter G is named

explanation.surface: The Devil urges someone to have a bet while in Bangkok.
explanation.walkthrough: A flutter is British slang for a small bet; the question mark admits the definition is a description of a coin rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The satang is a small Thai coin, a hundredth of a baht, the sort of money staked on a small wager.

clue.text: Tempers breaking records with ultimate in impatience

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of a word is its final one
a letter breaking a word splits it open and sits in the gap

blocks.note: annals are yearly historical records
last letter of impatience

explanation.surface: Impatient people lose their tempers and break records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tempers' reads as a noun in the surface but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To anneal metal or glass is to temper it, heating and cooling it slowly to toughen it.

clue.text: Brood maybe, gold or yellow parrots

definitions.note: Nestor is a genus name for a group of parrots

blocks.note: a nest can mean the brood of young in it
or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: A brood of gold or yellow parrots, as a birdwatcher might record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold or yellow' reads as a choice of colours, but or is the heraldic tincture meaning either of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestor is the genus of large New Zealand parrots, the kea and the kaka.

clue.text: Pay is half put on what you might call a flutter?

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word is a single letter, here the second
in a down entry, a piece put on another sits above it and comes first

blocks.note: the second half of is

blocks.clueFragment: what you might call a flutter?
blocks.note: alary means relating to wings, and a flutter is a wing movement

explanation.surface: Half of someone's pay goes on a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flutter' points to betting, as in 13 Across's Bangkok coin, but here it is the beating of wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A salary is fixed regular pay for a job.

clue.text: Number excluded from friendly relationship, opinionated

indicators.note: what is excluded is shut out, so that letter is removed from the longer word

blocks.note: an entente is a friendly understanding between nations
N stands for a number in algebra

explanation.surface: Someone opinionated is shut out of a friendly arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Entêté is French-derived for obstinate or headstrong, someone stubbornly set in their opinions.

clue.text: Little bird: short round maiden with oomph

indicators.note: one thing round another surrounds it

blocks.note: a short is a measure of spirits, and so is a tot
M is a maiden over in cricket scoring
it means sex appeal

explanation.surface: A small plump girl full of energy, likened to a little bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short round' reads as a description of the maiden, but short is a noun (a short drink) and round is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomtit is a small bird, especially the blue tit or other titmouse.

clue.text: Reduced, having retired, at being kept in

indicators.note: something kept in another is held inside it

blocks.note: someone who has retired for the night is abed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pensioner's income has fallen since retiring, while being kept indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests leaving work, but here it means gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Abated means lessened or diminished, the same as reduced.

clue.text: Crow's home? Fencing equipment after end of nest

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
the equipment comes after, so the single letter goes first

blocks.note: last letter of nest
an épée is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: A crow's nest, with fencing nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow' looks like the bird, and nest supports that, but it is the Crow people of the Great Plains.
explanation.definitionFit: A tepee is a conical tent used as a dwelling by Plains peoples such as the Crow.

clue.text: Some NW Italians, those voting against wearing suit

indicators.note: a person wearing a garment is inside it, so the word before goes within the next

blocks.note: gee is a dialect verb meaning to suit or fit
the noes are those voting no

explanation.surface: Northern Italian politicians in suits voting against a measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like clothing, which suits 'wearing', but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Genoese are the people of Genoa, a port city in north-west Italy.

clue.text: Ultimate for poet in grip of Eros, transported?

definitions.text: Ultimate for poet in grip of Eros, transported?

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of a word is the final one
something in another's grip is held inside it
transported means carried away, so the letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: the Greek god of love, taken as written
last letter of poet

explanation.surface: A poet in the grip of love is carried away into rapture.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a poet held by love and transported is in the grip of estro.
explanation.definitionFit: Estro is poetic enthusiasm or inspiration, the ultimate rapture a poet could hope for.

clue.text: Calf muscle, without another unserviceable

blocks.note: sole means only, with no other
u/s is the abbreviation of unserviceable

explanation.surface: An injured calf muscle, with no partner, has become useless.
explanation.definitionFit: The soleus is the flat muscle of the calf beneath the gastrocnemius, which flexes the foot.

clue.text: What's this seaweed for? Flavour when cooking

indicators.note: cooking works ingredients over, so the word before it is rearranged
asking what is left once a word is taken away means removing those letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters to take out

explanation.surface: A cook asks what this seaweed is used for: flavouring dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'what is this seaweed? Flavour, cooked, without for'. The question reads as a cook's query but hides a subtraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulva is the sea lettuce, a green seaweed with thin edible fronds.

clue.text: Good mimic that represents threat taking off Tory

indicators.note: taking off means removing, so those letters are stripped from the longer word

blocks.note: minatory means threatening
taken as written; a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A skilled impressionist mimics a threatening politician by imitating a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' suggests mimicry, which fits the mimic, but it means removing.
explanation.definitionFit: The mina or myna is an Asian starling famous for imitating human speech, so a good mimic.

clue.text: Nepali tat, a ton transported — one of many in Assam? (13, two words)

indicators.note: transported means carried off elsewhere, so the letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: the four words taken together as letters

explanation.surface: A ton of Nepalese junk is shipped across to Assam.
explanation.walkthrough: Assam is a state in north-east India famous for its tea; the question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is covered with estates growing tea, so a tea plantation is one of many found there.

clue.text: Gold surplus receding in rand vale (8, two words)

indicators.note: something receding goes back, so the word before it is read backwards

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a surplus is what is left over
i' is a shortened dialect form of in

explanation.surface: A gold surplus is shrinking in the South African currency valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vale' reads as a valley but is Latin for farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Au revoir is French for goodbye, and vale is the Latin word for farewell.

clue.text: Nothing's backed up when wife follows operating system

indicators.note: something backed up has moved backwards, so the word is read in reverse
the wife follows, so her letters come last

blocks.note: nil means nothing
ux is short for uxor, Latin for wife

explanation.surface: A computer complaint: nothing has been saved, with the wife using the system next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed up' sounds like saving computer files, which fits the surface, but it reverses the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Linux is a free, open-source operating system used on servers and desktop computers.

clue.text: Green paradise? Adam's description after arrival of Eve maybe

definitions.text: Adam's description after arrival of Eve maybe

blocks.note: first meaning: an environmentally ideal nation

blocks.clueFragment: Adam's description after arrival of Eve maybe
blocks.note: second meaning: a botanical word for lacking ribs, which Adam was after one was used to make Eve

explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Eve is made from Adam's rib, so afterwards he might be called ribless; that botanical sense is the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecostate would be an ecologically run state, while ecostate as a botanical adjective means without ribs.
